newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT- US T-bonds' short-term momentum faltering.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- US T-bonds' short-term momentum faltering.

text.p: Short-term momentum indicators for U.S. Treasury bond futures are faltering after a lengthy range trade following a sharp rally from the April lows, techncial analysts said.
Although June T-bond futures were likely to stay tethered to the 110 area for a little longer, they were beginning to show a downward bias, they added.
"Daily stochastics are beginning to wane and short-term, intraday oscillators are pushing lower from overbought (territory)," said Cia Lallas, a technical analyst at MMS International.
"If you can't get over 110-22/32 (Tuesday's high) within the next couple of sessions, you're probably due for a bigger correction," she added.
June bonds were off 8/32 at 110-2/32 at 1110 CDT/1610 GMT after rising to an early high of 110-16/32 and then slipping on news of a strong 2.6 pecent gain in April housing starts.

"Momentum indicators on the intraday charts were diverging negatively on the strength we saw prior to the number," noted Mathew Crosson, director of fixed income at Pegasus Econometrics Group. "The market had been rolling over to the downside even before the housing number."

He did not see the market diving much below 110 today but added that a close near 110 would form a "bearish engulfing" pattern that would confirm Thursday's ominous "hanging man" on the daily candlestick chart.

A hanging man is formed when the session has a small body near the top of its range with a long tail, more than twice the size of the body, dangling below. A bearish engulfing occurs when the session has a negative body that engulfs the previous day's body.
"This may be an indication of further downside movement," Crosson said.
However, analysts were generally positive on the mid- to long-term outlook.
"I think overall the charts still look good," Lallas said. "If you retest 109-8/32, which is the 38-percent retracement off of the April lows, I think it will be well supported."
Crosson said the uptrend would stay intact as long as June T-bonds stayed above 109-1/2 on a closing basis.

Analysts said 110 has acted like a magnet in recent weeks because of the 100- and 200-day moving aveages lurking in the area and the hefty open interest in the 110 strike price of June T-bond futures options, which expire at noon today.
In addition, traders have been wary of buying near the top of the recent ranges or selling near the lower end ahead of next Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Once those factors are removed next week, the market is likely to start showing a more trending-type movement, analysts said.
